## What happened

On 2026-04-11 from 13:42 to 15:09 UTC the web ACL example-shop-acl in front of shop-web-alb blocked about 235 requests per minute on POST /api/cart/coupon through the rate-based rule rate-limit-coupon (10 requests per 5 minutes per IP). 98.0% of all blocks in the window were this rule. The traffic came from 62 clients in one network (ASN 64511) with one TLS fingerprint, python-requests/2.31.0 as user agent, no session cookies, spread over four countries.

## Causal chain

1. Trigger: a group of 62 clients began POSTing to /api/cart/coupon at 13:42 UTC · Confirmed
2. The group is automated, not shoppers · Likely (weakest link)
3. Mechanism: rate-limit-coupon blocked 18,803 of their requests · Confirmed
4. Symptom: WAF Block responses (HTTP 403 by default) · Confirmed (blocks)
5. Customer impact: no sign of broad impact; at least one browser-shaped client outside the group was rate-limited at least 111 times · Likely

## What found it

The rule-level 60-second BlockedRequests series (W2-Q1) for the timing, then the S3 WAF logs of 13:40-15:15 (user_agents, fingerprints, header_shape, asns, countries; W3-Q6..Q12) for who.

## What did not help

ALB metrics (empty), ECS listings (empty), gh reads (empty) and CloudTrail (no WAF or ECS change); the 14-day recurrence pull covered only 7.5 days. Sampled requests were out of reach (incident older than 3 hours).

## Follow-ups raised

Check what the roughly 2,100 group requests that passed the limit got back; identify the one browser-shaped client that was rate-limited; consider stricter handling of non-browser fingerprints on the coupon path; consider an alarm on rate-limit-coupon blocks; add ALB and application log visibility.
